transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-04 14:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording ID: ff_20260904_LF_8472
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Victor Alvarez (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (LumenFold Head of Platform), Tom Reeves (Cloud Architect), Lena Park (Security Lead), Jae Kim (SRE)

Summary:
Brief: Discovery focused on private/VPC deployment for Redwood Private: VPC peering vs private endpoints, transit gateway design, egress controls, zero-trust posture, and regional constraints (EU / APAC). Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; primary interest in Private.

Topics:
- Network topology and peering options
- Private endpoints and NAT/egress handling
- Region gating and data residency (EU, APAC restrictions)
- Compliance (SOC2/ISO, KMS/HSM, audit logs)
- Authentication and SSO (SAML, SCIM provisioning)
- Timeline and success criteria for pilot

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros — I'm Maya Chen, account lead on Redwood.
[00:15] Aisha: Hi, this is Aisha, Head of Platform at LumenFold, we have Tom, Lena and Jae on who will drive the technical side.
[00:25] Tom: Hey all.
[00:30] Victor: Hi, Victor here, I’ll go deep on the network bits and the Private deployment options.
[00:40] Maya: Great, high level — we understand you're evaluating hosting options for your inference stack, primarily leaning towards Private because of data residency and zero trust. Can you walk us through current constraints?
[00:55] Aisha: Sure — we ingest customer ML telemetry, some PII-ish metadata, and regulators want EU-only processing for a subset of customers. We also have an internal security mandate to avoid public internet egress for model traffic.
[01:10] Lena: Yep, zero-trust is non-negotiable; all services must be reachable only over our VPCs, SAML SSO required, and keys must live in our KMS or HSM.
[01:22] Maya: Understood. Quick qual: are you open to Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated GPUs in our infra) or do you require full Private (customer VPC + Private endpoints / peering)?
[01:35] Aisha: Ideally Private in our VPC, but if Dedicated gives strong network isolation and we can place it in EU regions with egress controls, we might consider it. Need to understand tradeoffs.
[01:50] Victor: Ok, tradeoff summary: Dedicated gives reserved capacity and simpler onboarding — Redwood manages the infra, but you still route over controlled peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. Private (VPC colocated) puts control in your VPC — you manage routing, peering, and KMS integration. Latency is slightly better in Private if you colocate near your app subnets.
[02:15] Tom: For us latency is medium priority, security and egress are top. We want minimal outbound, ideally no direct internet calls for inference traffic. How does Redwood handle private endpoints and DNS?
[02:30] Victor: We support cloud provider private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink, GCP Private Service Connect). In AWS we can create interface endpoints in your VPC and register a private hosted zone so your hosts resolve the Redwood service to private IPs. For egress, we recommend routing model-serving egress through your NAT or egress GW where you can apply inspection.
[02:55] Jae: If we use PrivateLink, what about cross-account VPC peering/transit? Our setup uses Transit Gateway to stitch multiple accounts. We need to ensure traffic to Redwood doesn't require exposing routes to the public internet.
[03:12] Victor: PrivateLink works across TGW but you need to announce the endpoint and ensure route tables point to the endpoint ENIs. Alternatively, where PrivateLink is not feasible, we support VPC Peering or VPNs. We can also place a regional ingress plane in your account to avoid cross-region hops.
[03:30] Lena: KMS — can Redwood accept customer-managed keys? Our compliance team requires HSM-backed CMKs, rotation policies and no plaintext key export.
[03:42] Maya: Yes, for Private we have an integration path with customer KMS/HSM. We also support envelope encryption where keys are in your KMS and Redwood can't decrypt without your approval. I'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[03:55] Aisha: Good. Also curious about audit logs — need full request/response logs for inference calls or at least metadata to prove lineage. Storage location must be EU for certain customers.
[04:08] Victor: We can stream audit logs to your S3/GCS in your account in the region you choose or to a SOC 2 compliant workspace with region constraints. For Private, customers often collect logs directly into their logging buckets via S3 replication or Radix connectors.
[04:25] Tom: Any constraints around model uploads? We have large model artifacts — prefer pulling from our internal artifact repo instead of pushing to Redwood.
[04:36] Victor: We support model registry integrations and pulling over internal network if you host your artifacts in a reachable location within your VPC or via a secured endpoint. If you want to keep models entirely in your account, we can deploy model-serving components in your VPC that mount the model store.
[04:55] Aisha: Okay timeline question — we have an internal Q4 pilot goal. What does an ideal onboarding schedule look like?
[05:05] Maya: Typical pilot: week 0 prep (network checklist, creds), week 1 setup of private endpoints and test accounts, week 2 model onboarding + smoke tests, week 3 latency/cost benchmark, week 4 pilot go/no-go. So about 3–4 weeks if network is straightforward.
[05:25] Lena: We will need a security review before week 1; SOC2 docs and penetration test attestation are gating.
[05:34] Maya: Understood — I'll send SOC2 + ISO artifacts and our standard pen test summary.
[05:40] Tom: A few nitty details — we operate in eu-west-1 and europe-west4 (GCP). Do you support cross-cloud private endpoints? We need a multi-cloud presence.
[05:53] Victor: We do multi-region and multi-cloud. For GCP we use Private Service Connect and for AWS PrivateLink; we can provision endpoints in each region. If you want a unified control plane in your VPC, we can deploy lightweight agents to handle routing and KV cache affinity.
[06:10] Jae: About KV cache affinity — if sessions are sticky and we use multiple availability zones, how does Redwood keep KV cache local?
[06:20] Victor: We support session affinity and region-aware routing. When deployed in your VPC, we can pin customer traffic to specific nodes or use consistent hashing to reduce cross-AZ KV cache fetches. That improves tail latency.
[06:34] Aisha: Cost question — any surprises around egress or endpoint charges? We have to budget for interface endpoint hourly fees and data processing charges.
[06:44] Victor: Yes, AWS/Cloud provider charges for PrivateLink and NAT egress remain; Redwood's pricing covers inference compute and control plane. We'll include an estimate for expected endpoint charges based on your throughput. Victor: I'll include a cost appendix.
[06:58] Lena: About authentication — we need SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC aligned with our AD groups.
[07:08] Maya: Redwood supports SAML for SSO and SCIM provisioning. For Private deployments, you can push SAML assertions to the control plane in your account and we can map groups to RBAC roles.
[07:20] Tom: Is there an option to route only telemetry through Redwood and keep model weights on-prem? We may want a hybrid to reduce egress.
[07:30] Victor: Hybrid is common — models stay on-prem and we deploy lightweight inference shims that call local GPU pools. Alternatively, we can use Redwood Serving connected over private network to your model store; the key is ensuring the model pull path is private.
[07:46] Aisha: What about failover? If an EU region has an outage, do we want automatic fallback to a different region? That has data residency implications.
[07:58] Victor: We recommend defining fallback policies per-customer class. For EU-only customers you can disable cross-region fallback. For others you can define an ordered fallback list. Redwood's routing policy supports these rules.
[08:15] Jae: On the network side, we run strict egress ACLs — can Redwood's health checks and control plane traffic be routed through an egress proxy in our account?
[08:26] Victor: Yes, control plane heartbeats can be proxied. For Private we can put an outbound egress proxy in your account or configure VPC endpoints that allow control-plane communication without direct internet.
[08:38] (crosstalk)
[08:42] Maya: Quick check — any blockers right now to proceed to a technical deep dive? Tom?
[08:49] Tom: Not yet, but need concrete diagrams for TGW and PrivateLink behaviors. Also want a sample Terraform snippet for endpoint provisioning.
[08:58] Victor: I will draft Terraform examples.
[09:02] (long pause while sharing screen)
[09:20] Victor: I'm pulling up a sample topology — look for a small diagram where we create an interface endpoint in your account, attach to private hosted zone, and route through TGW to your app subnets. If you're using Transit Gateway, you may need route table entries to point to the endpoint ENIs.
[09:40] Tom: That makes sense. Does Redwood require any public IPs in the setup? We prefer none.
[09:49] Victor: No public IPs required for data plane calls. Control plane might use outbound connectivity; however in fully Private mode we can use a VPC peering + endpoint approach that removes public IPs entirely.
[09:59] Lena: Penetration test question — will Redwood accept a scheduled red-team? We need to include Redwood in scope for our upcoming audit.
[10:09] Maya: Yes, we can coordinate. We have a standard process for vendor pen tests; I'll share the process doc.
[10:15] Aisha: Good. A couple more items: do you have region gating to prevent model execution for EU-only customers from leaving EU?
[10:25] Victor: Yes, policy-based routing can pin inference execution to particular regions. We can tag customers and apply enforcement at the routing layer — this avoids cross-region fallback for EU-only tags.
[10:36] Jae: Any additional firewall/NACL recommendations? We typically lock down egress to specific endpoints and ports.
[10:45] Victor: We recommend allowing outbound to the interface endpoint IPs and control plane port ranges; we’ll provide a minimal ports list. Also recommend NAT for extra logging.
[10:56] (note: screen link to topology doc shared: https://redwood.docs/private-endpoint-topology (placeholder))
[11:05] Maya: I'll email that doc after the call.
[11:10] Tom: On commercial — pricing for Private is a bit of a question. We have unpredictable burst usage. Do you offer burst capacity on Dedicated or a buffering option?
[11:23] Maya: Yes, Dedicated has reserved baseline plus burst; Private can be configured similarly with autoscaling policies. We can propose a hybrid commit model for Q4 pilot to cap monthly costs while allowing some burst.
[11:35] Aisha: Good. Last question, any limits on model size or quantization? We want to run some 70B variants.
[11:46] Victor: We support large models; for on-prem GPU pools we'd need to validate memory footprint and kernel optimizations. For a 70B we typically recommend quantization profiles and shard-aware deployment. We'll need model details to advise.
[11:58] Maya: Ok, recap of next steps: Victor shares VPC checklist, Terraform snippet, cost appendix; Maya sends SOC2/ISO, SAML/SCIM files and pricing; LumenFold provides region list and egress inventory; schedule SE deep dive week of 2026-09-14.
[12:16] Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[12:20] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up by email with attachments.
[12:25] (meeting ends)

Action items (summary):
- Victor: VPC topology checklist, sample Terraform provision for PrivateLink/PSC, cost appendix (due 2026-09-08).
- Maya: SOC2/ISO document pack, SAML+SCIM integration guide, commercial/pricing summary (due 2026-09-07).
